name: outfit_swap_callsite_aob
notes: Inner mid-function site for the outfit-swap-in-combat patch (offset +13 is the 'mov r14b, al' that becomes 'xor r14d, r14d'). name: outfit_swap_callsite_context
notes: Same site as outfit_swap_callsite_aob (id 1004) extended 7 bytes upward to include the call-into-IsInCombat sequence ('mov rcx, [rax+0x90]; ...'). 23 bytes. Use as a more uniquely-positioned anchor when the 16-byte AOB feels too short.

name: IsInCombat_callsite_26b
notes: 26-byte sig for the IsInCombat() callsite prologue: 'mov rax, [rcx+8]; mov rcx, [rax+0x90]; add rcx, 0x0B60; mov rax, [rcx]; call qword ptr [rax+8]; cmp al, 2'. Pattern '48 8B 41 08 48 8B 88 90 00 00 00 48 81 C1 60 0B 00 00 48 8B 01 FF 50 08 3C 02'. Used by kcdx/examples/conflict-test-{hook-on-hook,hook-on-patch,patch-on-hook} as their hook target. RVA stored is the pattern-hit position; function entry is at RVA-4 (consumers using this as a function-entry anchor apply offset = -4, as in comp-02-hook-on-patch and the conflict-test mods). Verified against the binary.

name: IsInCombat_callsite_with_stack_frame
notes: 30-byte sig prefixed with 'sub rsp, 0x28' — a different call site to the same IsInCombat() vtable method from a calling routine with its own stack frame. Pattern '48 83 EC 28 48 8B 41 08 48 8B 88 90 00 00 00 48 81 C1 60 0B 00 00 48 8B 01 FF 50 08 3C 01' ends in `3C 01` (cmp al, 1), NOT `3C 02` (cmp al, 2). The `3C 02` variant is id 1006 at RVA 0x005605BC — two distinct call sites in WHGame.dll invoking the same IsInCombat() vtable slot but checking different combat-state thresholds (1 vs 2). Used by test-plugins/comp-03-hook-on-hook-A and -B for first-wins testing. Live-verified.

name: gEnv_pConsole_mov_instruction
notes: The 'mov rcx, [rip+pConsole]' instruction inside the autoexec-executor function. RVA derived by a three-step resolver: (1) find 'exec autoexec.cfg' string in .rdata; (2) scan .text for any `48 8D 15 ? ? ? ?` LEA and check RIP-relative target == string address; (3) check 7 bytes preceding the matched LEA: if `4C 8B 92 18 01 00 00`, the MOV is at LEA-0x17 (V1.4+ layout, used by KCD2 1.5); else the MOV is at LEA-7 (older). pConsole_ptr_VA = MOV_VA + 7 + disp32(MOV+3..6); gEnv_VA = pConsole_ptr_VA - 0xA8. NOT a single-pattern AOB — must be resolved via the anchor (id 1011) at runtime. Verified against the binary, consistent with a predecessor KCD project's shipping plugin on KCD2 1.4+.

name: gEnv_pConsole
notes: Static pointer slot in .data: gEnv->pConsole. Read this 8-byte pointer to get IConsole*. RVA derived by following the RIP-relative disp32 from id 1008. Will move per game build — Address Library updates it. Subtract 0xA8 to get gEnv base (id 1010).

name: gEnv
notes: Static SSystemGlobalEnvironment instance base (gEnv). Derived as id 1009 RVA - 0xA8. Plugins read fields at known offsets: pScriptSystem (+0x28), pCryPak (+0x50), pGame (+0x90), pConsole (+0xA8), etc. Verified against the binary.

name: string_exec_autoexec_cfg
notes: String literal 'exec autoexec.cfg' in .rdata. Single LEA xref in .text from inside the engine's autoexec executor. Use as the seed anchor when the gEnv resolver SIG needs to be re-derived after a game update — find this string, find its single LEA xref, walk backwards to the pConsole MOV. Lives in .rdata not .text — status reflects RVA stability for the lifetime of this game build.

name: IConsole_AddCommand
notes: IConsole::AddCommand(const char* sCommand, ConsoleCommandFunc func, int nFlags, const char* sHelp). __thiscall (rcx=IConsole*). Callback ABI: void __fastcall (IConsoleCmdArgs*). **vtable[33]** (NOT slot 32 — the canonical CryEngine ordering is swapped in this build). Originally recorded as slot 32 from a vtable dump; corrected against the binary, which showed slot 32 is the script-string overload. Three independent confirmations: (a) slot 33's body stores r8 raw at record [+0x20]; slot 32 runs r8 through CryString-assign at 0x1804f6ac8; (b) slot 33's duplicate-registration error says 'console command [%s] is already registered' while slot 32 says 'script command [%s] is already registered'; (c) the engine's own static wrapper at 0x180B99098 (used to register playerGoto / freeze / etc.) calls vtable[33] via [pConsole->vtable + 0x108]. Verified against the binary.

name: IConsole_RemoveCommand
notes: IConsole::RemoveCommand(const char* sName). __thiscall. vtable[34]. Verified against the binary; small function body matches the expected map-erase shape. Used for [[command]] cleanup on plugin unload (if/when v0.2 supports unload). -> bool (success flag; SETNZ BL / MOV AL,BL before RET — the engine returns the map-erase result, diverging from the canonical CryEngine 'void RemoveCommand' header; the return type is empirically probed against the binary, not assumed from a header). Confirmed by a body-wide analysis against the binary.

name: IConsole_ExecuteString
notes: IConsole::ExecuteString(const char* command, bool bSilentMode, bool bDeferExecution). __thiscall. vtable[35]. Verified against the binary. Useful for plugins that want to programmatically execute console commands (e.g., binding a hotkey to a console command via Lua). -> void (entry-point 0x007A5818 and helper 0x007A586C both return with no eax/rax write — pure register-restore before RET; matches the canonical CryEngine header, binary-verified).
signature: void (ptr self, cstr command, bool bSilentMode, bool bDeferExecution)

name: IConsole_GetCVar
notes: IConsole::GetCVar(const char* name) -> ICVar*. __thiscall. vtable[23]. Verified against the binary (canonical CryEngine slot). Underpins kcdx.get_cvar_bool / get_cvar_int / get_cvar_float (Lua surface) and the C-side CVar lookup.

name: IConsole_AddCommand_static_wrapper
notes: Engine-side static function that resolves pConsole from its known .data slot and calls vtable[33] (AddCommand func-overload). Signature: void __fastcall(const char* name, ConsoleCommandFunc func, int nFlags, const char* sHelp). Used by the engine's own boot-time registrations (playerGoto, freeze, etc.). Plugins may prefer this over directly calling AddCommand because (a) no need to fetch pConsole first, (b) survives vtable shuffles across game patches as long as the wrapper itself stays at this RVA. Registers a console command whose body is a Lua source string (e.g., "Game.Connect(%1)"). Plugins typically want id 2000 (function-pointer form) instead, but this is documented for completeness.

Verified against the binary: body does path strlen + 0x800 cap + mode-string parse; a body-wide stack-arg analysis confirms 4-arg fastcall, flags 32-bit; 12+ call sites pass (path, mode rb/wb/ab/wt/w+b, flags); sibling slots +0x148 FWrite, +0x1B8 FClose.

name: gEnv_pCryPak

See docs/mod-loader-absorb.md.

name: ModManager_Select
notes: wh::C_ModManager SELECTION driver (FUN_180da104c) — the mod-loader absorb hook target. __fastcall void(C_ModManager* this) — this-only, void return (a body-wide stack-arg analysis shows the prologue reads only [rcx+0x18/0x20/0x30/0x38] member fields, no incoming stack arg). Stage 1 of the engine mod-load: clears the enabled list (this+0x30..0x38) + scanned list (this+0x18..0x20), Steam-workshop scan, alphabetical mods/ scan (FUN_180da1178), per-mod manifest validate (FUN_18243e7b8, 0x70 stride), mod_order.txt select+order (FUN_180da1294); fallback enables all scanned in scan order if no mod_order.txt. Invoked synchronously from the ctor FUN_180da0eb0; reached by DIRECT call from CSystem::Init (FUN_1807a6c64 @ 0x1807A76FE), NOT in any vtable. LIVE-CONFIRMED against the binary: a detour at this RVA fired from the worker thread BEFORE CSystem::Init completed mod selection — worker-thread install is in time for the narrow takeover. See docs/mod-loader-absorb.md.

name: ModManager_ctor
notes: wh::C_ModManager ctor/factory (FUN_180da0eb0). ABI: undefined8* (undefined8* outResult /*rcx*/, CSystem* sys /*rdx*/, CryString* modsDir /*r8*/) — 3-arg fastcall. Allocates a 0x68-byte C_ModManager, sets vptr=wh::C_ModManager::vftable, stores sys at +8 and modsDir at +0x10, zero-inits the mod lists (+0x18..+0x58), registers console cmd wh_mod_GenerateReport, then calls the SELECTION driver FUN_180da104c (id 3100). The object is stored into CSystem at the mod-manager registry slot (CSystem+0x2B30) so stage 2 + downstream find it. Reached by direct call from CSystem::Init @ 0x1807A76FE. Confirmed against the binary by a capstone E8-sweep (the Ghidra xref DB showed 0 refs — inner workers dispatch via member-fn-ptr std::function). See docs/mod-loader-absorb.md.
signature: ptr (ptr outResult, ptr sys, ptr modsDir)

name: ModManager_Mount
notes: wh::C_ModManager MOUNT driver (FUN_1804d9058) — stage 2 of the engine mod-load. ABI: void(C_ModManager* modMgr /*rcx*/, CryString* modsDir /*rdx*/) — 2-arg fastcall. Constructs a std::_Func_impl_no_alloc<lambda, void, wh::I_Mod const&> (the per-mod OpenPacks lambda FUN_181ddc920) then iterates the ENABLED wh::I_Mod list (modMgr+0x30) invoking the lambda per mod. The lambda gets the pak system via *(*(modMgr+8 /*=CSystem*/)+0x228) and calls OpenPacks (pak-mgr vtable slot +0x48 = slot 9, the wildcard plural mount) with (modDataDir, '<modPath>/*.pak', 0x10400, 0). Called once from CSystem::Init @ 0x1807A7F1C, later than the ctor (separated by unrelated engine init). The narrow takeover does NOT detour this — kcdx populates the enabled list in its order and lets this native MOUNT run verbatim (so localization/table-patch/mod.cfg passes are not silently dropped). Capstone E8-sweep confirmed. See docs/mod-loader-absorb.md.

name: ModManager_ReadModOrder
notes: wh::C_ModManager mod_order.txt reader / selection driver (FUN_180da1294). ABI: undefined1(C_ModManager* this /*rcx*/) -> bool (1 if mod_order.txt opened, else 0). Opens <modsDir>/mod_order.txt via the shared CCryFile helper FUN_1804605bc at nFlags 0x10006; on hit reads it line-by-line (strips '#' comments, trims), matches each line against the scanned-mod records (this+0x18..0x20, stride 0x70), appends matches to the enabled list (this+0x30) IN FILE ORDER, logs '[Mod] %d mods enabled'. => mod_order.txt line order == enabled-list order == mount order. This is the INPUT the absorb subsumes: kcdx reads mod_order.txt as the vanilla baseline ordering, merges kcdx-plugins/ + [load_order] on top, and writes the resolved order back to BOTH load_order.toml and mod_order.txt. See docs/mod-loader-absorb.md.

name: ModManager_ParseManifest
notes: wh::C_ModManager per-mod mod.manifest parse + version-gate (FUN_18243e7b8, image-base 0x180000000 + RVA 0x243E7B8). ABI: (modRecord* /*rcx*/). Reads mod.manifest (string @0x183DBE180), validates the modid + the <version>/game-version gate (version-string comparisons in sibling FUN_182440c6c). Owns error strings '[Mod] %s not found', 'Mod %s has invalid ModId', '[Mod] %s has bad format', '[Mod] %s has no version restrictions in manifest'. Populates the 0x70-byte I_Mod record string fields (path/id/name/description/author/version/date — see docs/mod-loader-absorb.md field map). The narrow takeover REUSES this (lets native SELECT run) so kcdx-built records get the engine's own manifest parse + real vtables for free; kcdx only re-orders + appends. Capstone-confirmed via string anchors. See docs/mod-loader-absorb.md.

name: ImodVtable_primary
notes: The wh::I_Mod concrete-class PRIMARY vtable (record offset +0x00). NOTE: this is the ADDRESS OF THE VTABLE (a data RVA to write into a synthesized record's +0x00 slot), NOT a vtable index (cf. the 3000-band index convention). The mod-loader absorb builds I_Mod records from scratch and must set this at +0x00 so native MOUNT + downstream passes dispatch correctly. LIVE-VERIFIED against the binary across two boots: all 15 enabled records carry this identical vtable, and the VA-base resolves to this same RVA on both boots (ASLR-stable; two distinct load bases 0x7FF8FF470000 + 0x7FF8FF000000 both yield 0x46AAF00). name: ImodVtable_subobject

ADDRESS OF THE VTABLE (data RVA for the synthesized record's +0x18 slot), NOT a vtable index. Paired with ImodVtable_primary (id 3105); the absorb sets both when building a from-scratch I_Mod record. LIVE-VERIFIED against the binary, identical across all 15 records on two boots, ASLR-stable to RVA 0x46AAED8; fn pointers read as real code. See docs/mod-loader-absorb.md.

name: C_ModManager_vtable
notes: The wh::C_ModManager concrete-class primary vtable base address. ADDRESS OF THE VTABLE (a data RVA written into the synthesized C_ModManager at +0x00), NOT a vtable index (cf. the 3000-band index convention). Same kind as ImodVtable_primary (3105) / ImodVtable_subobject (3106): a vtable base address, not a slot integer. 8 function pointers, all classified as code in both boots of the live ctor_probe (boot 1 + boot 2 of _research/init-cycle-recon, ctor_probe.cpp), ASLR-stable across two distinct load bases. Discovered by reading the C_ModManager ctor disassembly: lea rax, [rip + 0x2d01f67] at site 0x180da0ef9 -> 0x180da0ef9 + 7 + 0x2d01f67 = 0x183AA2E60; image base 0x180000000 -> RVA 0x3AA2E60. The mod-loader absorb work ("narrow takeover" / replacement ctor) needs this to set [modmgr+0x00] correctly when building a C_ModManager from scratch. Verified against the binary.

name: WHGame_allocator
notes: WHGame allocator. Called by the C_ModManager ctor at site 0x180da0ed4 to allocate the 0x68-byte heap block that becomes the C_ModManager (see _research/init-cycle-recon/FINDINGS.md). Body verified by capstone disassembly of the live DLL (2026-05-28): reads rcx as the size arg (mov rbx, rcx); calls an indirect allocator via a static fn-ptr slot (mov rax, [rip + 0x4fa3c42]; call rax); returns the allocated heap pointer in rax (passed through unchanged); does accounting (lock add/inc on rip-relative counters near 0x4ce62*). The replacement ctor in the absorb work uses this allocator so WHGame's own destructor (if it ever runs against a kcdx-built record) frees through the matching pair.

name: CryString_placement_construct
notes: CryString placement-construct (refcount-aware copy ctor). Called by the C_ModManager ctor at site 0x180da0f09 with rcx = &[modmgr+0x10] (the in-place CryString destination) and rdx = a source CryStringT* on the stack. Body verified by capstone disassembly of the live DLL (2026-05-28): reads dest in rcx (mov rbx, rcx); reads the source's data ptr via [rdx]; steps back 0xC bytes to reach the source's CryString header (sub rcx, 0xc); validates via an internal helper (calls 0x1823ec8c8); on success, copies the source's data ptr to dest (mov [rbx], rax) AND atomically bumps the source header's refcount (lock inc [rax-0xc]) -- the canonical CryString copy-on-write copy-ctor. Returns rax = rbx (the dest). The replacement ctor uses this to construct the in-place 'mods' CryString at +0x10 from the stack-local CryString built by id 3110 (CryString_init_from_string).

name: CryString_init_from_string
notes: CryString init-from-cstr (named tmp_name_init in earlier recon work; the C_ModManager ctor uses it to build a stack-local CryString from the modsDir cstr arg before the placement-construct at id 3109 finalizes the in-place CryString at modmgr+0x10). Called by the ctor at site 0x180da0eed with rcx = a stack-local CryString dest and rdx = the modsDir cstr. Body verified by capstone disassembly of the live DLL (2026-05-28): reads rcx (mov rsi, rcx -- dest) and rdx (mov rdi, rdx -- source cstr); runs an inline strlen on rdi (or rbx, -1; inc rbx; cmp byte ptr [rdi+rbx], 0; jne); allocates len+0xD bytes for the CryString header + buffer + null terminator; writes the header (refcount=1, length, alloc-size); copies the cstr into the buffer; sets *dest = newbuf+0xC (the CryStringT pointer points past its header). Returns rax = rsi (the dest). See _research/init-cycle-recon/FINDINGS.md follow-up #4.
